_comment: Files with jsx-a11y/control-has-associated-label violations. eslint.config.js reads this list and downgrades the rule to a warning FOR THESE FILES ONLY, so a violation in any other file is an error and fails `npm run lint`. The list may only SHRINK: src/test/a11y_debt_is_accurate.test.ts fails if a listed file has no violations left (delete its entry) or if a listed file no longer exists. An entry that describes nothing is how a ratchet stops being one. F172.
_shape: The 138 measured on 2026-09-13 were described as 'icon-only buttons without an accessible name'. Classified with the same parser eslint uses, exactly ONE was a button: input 108, textarea 17, div 5, td 4, th 2, button 1, option 1. Sixteen more were false positives of a kind worth knowing about - a control carrying id="x" with a sibling <label htmlFor="x">, which is correctly labelled at runtime and unresolvable by a static rule. Clear those by giving the label an id and the control aria-labelledby, never by copying the text into an aria-label that can drift from what is on screen (WCAG 2.5.3). The remaining 121 are controls with no accessible name at all, and are real.
_triage: Triaged one by one on 2026-09-15, because 'known limitation of one rule' is a label that hides a real defect. jsx-a11y/control-has-associated-label looks DOWN into a control's own children for text; it never looks UP at a wrapping <label>, and it does not follow htmlFor/id across this shape. Seventeen of the eighteen findings are therefore its blind spot and the code is CORRECT — e.g. <label>Start Date <input type="date"/></label> (ReplayPage), <label htmlFor={`journal-notes-${id}`}>Notes</label> with the matching <textarea id=...> (TradeJournal), a radio inside a <label> carrying the option text (FinancialSection), and a <td> inside an aria-hidden skeleton row (DataTable). Do NOT clear those with an aria-label: it would duplicate text already on screen and drift at the first rename (WCAG 2.5.3). The eighteenth was real and is FIXED: superadmin/ui.tsx's Toggle rendered div[role="switch"] inside a <label>, and a <label> implicitly labels only LABELABLE elements (input, select, textarea, button, meter, output, progress) — so all 64 uses announced as "switch, off" with no name, several of them controlling how the platform trades. It now carries aria-labelledby pointing at the element that renders the visible text, plus aria-describedby and aria-disabled. See src/test/the_superadmin_toggle_has_a_name.test.tsx.
